content: The text provided is a list of references and summaries of studies related to tuberculosis (TB) and its management, particularly in high TB incidence settings and among vulnerable populations. 1. Ma et al. conducted a longitudinal study in Kampala, Uganda, to investigate the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of individuals resistant to Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection within household contact settings. The study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2014. 2. Rathi et al. examined the prevalence and risk factors associated with tuberculin skin test positivity among household contacts of smear-positive pulmonary TB cases in Umerkot, Pakistan. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2002. 3. Lienhardt et al. identified risk factors for TB infection in sub-Saharan Africa through a contact study conducted in The Gambia. The results were published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 2003. 4. Jones-Lopez et al. explored the dynamics of TB transmission and the discordance between tuberculin skin tests (TST) and interferon-gamma release assays (IGRA) by analyzing cough aerosol cultures of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Their study was published in PLoS One in 2015. 5. Kifai and Bakari assessed Mantoux skin test reactivity among household contacts of HIV-infected and HIV-uninfected patients with sputum smear-positive TB in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. The findings were published in the East African Journal of Public Health in 2009. 6. Nunn et al. investigated the impact of HIV-1 infection on the infectiousness of TB in a study published in Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 1994. 7. Espinal et al. conducted a prospective study to evaluate the infectiousness of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in HIV-1-infected patients with TB. The study was published in The Lancet in 2000. 8. Hesseling et al. reported highly discordant T-cell responses in individuals recently exposed to household TB. Their findings were published in Thorax in 2009. 9. Guwatudde et al. studied TB prevalence among household contacts of infectious cases in Kampala, Uganda, with results published in the American Journal of Epidemiology in 2003. 10. The WHO consolidated guidelines on TB prevention recommend systematic screening and treatment for latent TB infection (LTBI) in high-risk populations, particularly children under 5 years who are household contacts of TB cases in high-incidence countries. 11. Lees et al. conducted a ten-year survey on pulmonary TB among household contacts, with findings published in Diseases of the Chest in 1961. 12. Ahmad Khan et al. evaluated the performance of symptom-based TB screening among people living with HIV, highlighting its limitations. The study was published in AIDS in 2014. 13. Nguyen et al. assessed the yield of chest radiography in TB screening for HIV-infected individuals at a district-level clinic. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2016. 14. Den Boon et al. evaluated the effectiveness of symptom and chest radiographic screening in TB prevalence surveys, with results published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2006. 15. The Ministry of Health reported on the national TB prevalence survey conducted in 2009–2010, providing critical data for TB control programs. 16. Van’t Hoog et al. examined the value of chest radiography and symptom screening strategies in TB prevalence surveys, with findings published in PLoS One in 2012. 17. Kapata et al. reported the results of Zambia’s first national TB prevalence survey conducted in 2013–2014, published in PLoS One in 2016. 18. Kebede et al. presented findings from Ethiopia’s first population-based national TB prevalence survey conducted in 2010–2011, published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2014. 19. Senkoro et al. reported the prevalence of pulmonary TB in Tanzania’s adult population based on a national survey conducted in 2012, with findings published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2016. 20. Law et al. conducted the first national TB prevalence survey in Lao PDR (2010–2011), with results published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2015. 21. Adetifa et al. reported on a nationwide TB prevalence survey in Gambia conducted in 2012, with findings published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2016. 22. Ayles et al. investigated the prevalence of TB, HIV, and respiratory symptoms in two Zambian communities, highlighting implications for TB control in the HIV era. The study was published in PLoS One in 2009. 23. Corbett et al. evaluated the diagnostic value of provider-initiated symptom screening for TB in Zimbabwe, considering the effect of HIV status. The findings were published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2010. 24. Datta et al. conducted a TB survey in a tribal population in North Arcot District, with results published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2001. 25. Gopi et al. conducted a baseline survey on TB prevalence in a South Indian community at the start of a DOTS program, with findings published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2003. 26. Mathad et al. investigated the association between quantitative IFN-gamma and IL-2 responses and latent TB test discordance in HIV-infected pregnant women. The study was published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 2016. 27. Rangaka et al. conducted a randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of isoniazid plus antiretroviral therapy in preventing TB. The study was published in The Lancet in 2014. 28. Mahomed et al. compared the predictive value of the tuberculin skin test and QuantiFERON-TB Gold for TB disease in adolescents in South Africa. The study was published in PLoS One in 2011. 29. McCarthy et al. highlighted the high incidence of latent TB infection among South African healthcare workers, calling for urgent action. The findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2015. 30. Sharma et al. compared TST and IGRA for diagnosing latent TB infection in high TB-burden settings, with findings published in PLoS One in 2017. 31. Spyridis et al. evaluated the effectiveness of different isoniazid-based regimens for treating latent TB infection in children, with results published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2007. 32. Galli et al. presented epidemiological and clinical data on pediatric TB in Italian children, based on the Italian Register of Pediatric Tuberculosis. The study was published in the International Journal of Molecular Sciences in 2016. 33. Van Zyl et al. investigated adherence to anti-TB chemoprophylaxis and treatment in children, with findings published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2006. 34. Menzies et al. compared the safety and efficacy of four months of rifampin versus nine months of isoniazid for latent TB infection in adults. The study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2018. 35. Diallo et al. assessed the safety and side effects of rifampin versus isoniazid in children, with findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2018. 36. Menzies et al. evaluated adverse events associated with rifampin and isoniazid therapy for latent TB infection in a randomized trial. The study was published in the Annals of Internal Medicine in 2008. 37. Swindells et al. investigated the efficacy of one month of rifapentine plus isoniazid in preventing HIV-related TB. The study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2019. 38. Martins et al. explored new regimens for preventing TB in adults with HIV infection, with findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2011. 39. Sterling et al. evaluated the efficacy of three months of weekly rifapentine and isoniazid for treating latent TB infection in HIV-coinfected individuals. The study was published in AIDS in 2016. 40. Villarino et al. conducted a randomized clinical trial to assess a three-month, 12-dose regimen of rifapentine and isoniazid for preventing TB in children and adolescents. The study was published in JAMA Pediatrics in 2015. 41. Gupta et al. examined the safety and efficacy of isoniazid preventive therapy in HIV-infected pregnant and postpartum women. The study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2019. 42. Kalk et al. reviewed the safety and effectiveness of isoniazid preventive therapy in HIV-infected pregnant women on antiretroviral therapy in routine care. The findings were published in Reproductive Toxicology in 2018. 43. Salazar-Austin et al. investigated the impact of isoniazid preventive therapy on pregnancy outcomes in HIV-infected women in the Tshepiso cohort. The study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2019. 44. Taylor et al. examined pregnancy outcomes in HIV-infected women receiving long-term isoniazid prophylaxis for TB and antiretroviral therapy. The study was published in Infectious Diseases in Obstetrics and Gynecology in 2013. 45. Seddon et al. designed a phase III cluster randomized controlled trial (TB-CHAMP) to evaluate levofloxacin versus placebo for preventing TB disease in child contacts of multidrug-resistant TB cases. The study protocol was published in Trials in 2018. 46. Fox et al. developed a protocol for the VQUIN MDR trial to assess levofloxacin versus placebo for treating latent TB among contacts of multidrug-resistant TB patients. The study was published in BMJ Open in 2020.
